recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. The current source satisfies FHIR-5949 and the later FHIR-39319 refinement; reintroducing the older DSTU1 phrasing would be redundant and potentially misleading.
issue_request: FHIR-5949 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request for DSTU1 MedicationPrescription asking how dosage.text relates to dosage.Scheduled[x]/dosage.timing. The accepted resolution required clarifying DosageInstruction.text and DosageInstruction.timing so text is expected for human display and reflects timing when both are populated.
initial_application: Historical commit 043ff8db6bacc9b4d846d3b0b5d1fd9f62730003 explicitly applied #5949 by updating the MedicationOrder/DosageInstruction spreadsheet wording. Later history renamed DosageInstruction to Dosage and MedicationPrescription/MedicationOrder to MedicationRequest, carrying the rule into the current datatype model.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Dosage as an active normative datatype and maps the legacy DosageInstruction name to Dosage. Later FHIR-39319 clarified that Dosage.text is a complete free-text dosage/SIG representation, and that fix is already present on the combined branch as bc5a413c8883a027335f4fba439c69659e7f3dc6. Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-5949 community evidence that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. source/datatypes/dosage.xml already says Dosage.text is a complete representation and should represent structured SIG data including timing, while Dosage.timing says Dosage.text should reflect timing content when both are populated.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive Pharmacy clarification that Dosage.text is a complete free-text dosage/SIG representation; already fixed on the combined branch and used to interpret the current wording.
